preconditions.description: The input integer n must be between 2 and 100 inclusive, representing the number of vertices in the tree.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= v <= n and 1 <= u <= n and v != u for v, u in edges)
preconditions.description: The input must contain exactly n-1 edges, each connecting two distinct vertices in the range [1, n]. The edges must form a tree (connected and acyclic).

preconditions.expression: all(v != u for v, u in edges)
preconditions.description: No edge in the input connects a vertex to itself (v ≠ u).

postconditions.expression: len(output_line.split()) == n and all(0 <= int(x) <= 1000000006 for x in output_line.split())
postconditions.description: The output must be a single line containing exactly n space-separated integers, each representing the count of labeled trees with n vertices sharing exactly i-1 edges with Will's tree (for i from 1 to n), modulo 1000000007.

postconditions.expression: stdout == ' '.join(str(count) for count in [sum(1 for tree in all_trees if shared_edges(tree, will_tree) == k) % 1000000007 for k in range(n)])
postconditions.description: For each k in 0..n-1, the k-th output integer (0-based index) is the number of labeled trees with n vertices that share exactly k edges with Will's tree, modulo 1000000007. Here, `all_trees` is the set of all labeled trees on n vertices, and `shared_edges(tree1, tree2)` is the number of edges common to both trees.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= k <= n - 1 and sum(counts) == total_trees for k, counts in enumerate([int(x) for x in output_line.split()]) if k == n - 1)
postconditions.description: The sum of all output integers must equal the total number of labeled trees on n vertices (Cayley's formula: n^(n-2)), modulo 1000000007, as every labeled tree must share some number of edges with Will's tree.
